handoff: Review: AC1–AC5 met with S1 integration tests, AC6 evidence checked; suite (394) and typecheck green. Three non-blocking points (silent skip of unreadable pushed slice file, per-story fetch in pick-list, dummy applies).

findings.title: An unreadable pushed slice file is silently skipped
findings.detail:
startedSliceBranches treats a slice file whose frontmatter fails to parse as not started (`fm = doc.ok ? … : null` then skipped), so B42's branch check passes it by and the problem only shows later, if at all. AGENTS.md S1/S2: a failing file is never guessed; pushedStory itself refuses story_corrupt for the same case.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Refuse (story_corrupt, naming the file on the branch) as pushedStory does.

findings.title: The pick-list fetches once per story branch on the remote
findings.detail:
closedStories calls pushedStory per key, each doing its own git fetch; with many story branches the interactive `norn story reopen` waits on N sequential fetches, and one corrupt story.md anywhere refuses the whole list.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Fetch the story branches in one call (one refspec per branch) and skip-with-note an unreadable record in the list rather than refusing it.

findings.title: `applies: () => false` is a placeholder required by TargetRule
findings.detail:
With `candidates` set, `applies` is documented as unused, yet every such rule must supply a dummy.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Make TargetRule a union (applies | candidates) or `applies` optional when candidates is given.
